A severe northeaster snowstorm produced extreme cold conditions; an 85-year-old male with Alzheimer disease wandered outdoors and was exposed to those conditions for approximately one hour, resulting in fatal hypothermia.

Radiological dispersal device detonation destroyed the decedent's home via blast-force structural collapse; the decedent sustained massive head and multiple traumatic injuries and died immediately at the scene.

Moore tornado outbreak created an immediate life-threatening hazard, compelling the 13-year-old decedent to rush down basement stairs to seek shelter; she fell approximately 15 steps headfirst, sustaining a right parietal epidural hematoma and skull fracture, leading to death. The tornado's physical forces did not directly contact the decedent; the fatal injury resulted from a fall during fleeing to shelter, which is an indirect disaster death.

The Northridge earthquake caused a chlorine tank pipe to crack at a water treatment facility, releasing chlorine gas; a 33-year-old worker with pre-existing asthma inhaled the gas, developed acute respiratory distress, and died at a hospital.

Detonation of an improvised nuclear device caused whole-body ionizing radiation exposure (8 Gy) resulting in acute radiation syndrome with bone marrow failure and neutropenia, leading to gram-negative sepsis and death on day 23.
